name: Heirloom Vine Tomatoes
description: Richly fragrant, sun-ripened heritage tomatoes grown with ancestral seeds. Deep red, juicy flesh packed with authentic garden sweetness and balanced acidity.
storageTip: Store stem-down at room temperature away from direct sunlight. Never refrigerate before fully ripe to preserve aroma and sweetness.

name: Baby Spinach & Red Sorrel
description: Tender, iron-rich emerald spinach leaves picked in early mist. Pairs mild nutty greens with zesty lemon-tinged red sorrel shoots.
storageTip: Wrap loosely in dry unbleached paper towels inside an airtight container in the vegetable crisper drawer for up to 7 days.

name: Sindhri Golden Mangoes
description: The crowned jewel of local orchards. Exceptionally sweet, velvety, fiber-free golden flesh with a heady tropical perfume picked tree-ripe from Mirpur Khas.
storageTip: Keep at room temperature until fragrant and slightly soft to gentle touch. Chill for one hour before slicing and serving.

name: Tender Crispy Okra (Bhindi)
description: Small, tender green pods harvested at daybreak in Malir. Extremely fresh and snap-crisp, perfect for dry-spiced pan fry or savory stews.
storageTip: Keep dry in a perforated paper bag in your refrigerator crisper. Only wash immediately before slicing and cooking.

name: Fresh Coriander & Spearmint
description: Intensely aromatic freshly bundled herb bouquets. Vibrant green sprigs of sweet mountain mint and sharp coriander with rooted stems.
storageTip: Trim stem ends and place standing upright in a jar with an inch of fresh water, covered loosely with a reusable cloth or silicone bag.

name: Sweet Pink Guavas (Amrood)
description: Fragrant round guavas with tender pink cores and crunchy pale exteriors. Bursting with floral sweet fragrance and tangy notes.
storageTip: Ripen on the counter until they give off a heady floral aroma. Once ripe, store in the fridge for up to 4 days.

name: Farm Fresh Pasture Eggs
description: Unwashed farm eggs gathered every morning from pasture-roaming Desi hens. Feature thick protective shells and deep amber-orange yolks.
storageTip: Store pointed end down in carton in the main refrigerator body (not door shelves) to maintain steady chill.

name: Raw Wildflower & Sidr Honey
description: Unfiltered, unpasteurized monofloral honey sustainably harvested from wild jujube (Sidr) groves. Rich butterscotch flavor with natural pollen crystals.
storageTip: Store at ambient room temperature in a dark pantry. Never refrigerate; gentle warming in a bowl of warm water decrystallizes honey.

name: Genovese & Sweet Thai Basil
description: Deep emerald leaves with sweet anise and peppery cloves notes. Grown without chemicals, hand-clipped just before morning market display.
storageTip: Like flowers, keep stems in a cup of water on the kitchen counter. Refrigeration turns basil leaves black.

name: Hydroponic Butterhead Lettuce
description: Soft, buttery green heads grown in pristine closed-loop mineral water systems. Sold with living roots attached for extraordinary lasting crispness.
storageTip: Keep roots immersed in shallow water or store in sealed container in the fridge with a slightly damp paper towel.

name: Artisanal Aged Goat Feta
description: Tangy, crumbly white cheese handcrafted in small batches using whole goat milk and sea salt brine. Creamy mouthfeel with a pleasant herbal finish.
storageTip: Keep submerged in original whey brine inside a sealed glass jar in your refrigerator.

name: Crunchy Red Radishes & Baby Turnips
description: Crisp scarlet globes with snow-white interiors and peppery bite. Freshly plucked with edible, vitamin-dense leafy greens intact.
storageTip: Remove green tops immediately upon arriving home to prevent roots from losing moisture. Store roots in cold water in fridge.

name: Cold-Pressed Raw Mustard Oil
description: Traditional wooden-ghani pressed yellow mustard seed oil. Pungent, deeply warming aroma with natural antioxidants preserved without heat processing.
storageTip: Keep in an opaque amber glass bottle in a cool cupboard away from sunlight to prevent oxidation.

name: Stone-Milled Whole Chakki Atta
description: Slowly stone-ground organic heritage wheat preserving the wheat germ, bran, and essential endosperm oils for fluffy, nutty, aromatic rotis.
storageTip: Keep in a cool dry steel tin or airtight container. For long storage, can be kept refrigerated.

name: Juicy Kinnow & Mandarin Oranges
description: Vibrant orange winter citrus from family groves. Renowned for extremely high juice content, vivid aroma, and tangy-sweet refreshing profile.
storageTip: Keep in a cool fruit bowl for up to 7 days, or in the fruit drawer of the refrigerator for up to 3 weeks.

name: Wood-Fired Wild Sourdough Boule
description: Crusty artisan bread fermented for 36 hours using a wild 8-year-old starter culture. Blistered golden crust with an airy, open, chewy crumb.
storageTip: Keep cut-side down on a wooden breadboard or in a linen bag. Do not store in plastic or refrigerator which stales bread.

name: Sweet Red Strawberries
description: Fragrant ruby red berries grown along riverbanks. Hand-picked ripe each morning, bursting with intense sweetness and natural fragrance.
storageTip: Store unwashed in a single layer with a dry paper towel in a breathable container in the fridge. Wash right before snacking.

name: Cultured Golden Buffalo Butter
description: Traditionally churned and slowly cultured white and golden farm butter. Rich, silky, slightly tangy taste unmatched for warm parathas and toast.
storageTip: Keep in a ceramic butter bell at room temperature for daily spreading, or wrap tightly in parchment paper in the freezer.

name: Tender Malir Ridge Gourds (Tori)
description: Crisp, slender emerald gourds picked at dawn in Malir fertile orchards. Exceptionally light, cooling, and mild for homestyle stews.
storageTip: Wrap in dry cotton cloth and store in the crisper drawer of your refrigerator for up to 5 days.

name: Crisp Desi Red Carrots (Gajar)
description: Deep red, intensely sweet heirloom winter carrots pulled fresh from alluvial soil. Unmatched for halwa, fresh morning juice, and winter salads.
storageTip: Cut off the green tops and keep submerged in a container of cold water in the fridge to preserve maximum crunch.

name: Sweet Bell Peppers & Pimentos
description: Crisp, thick-walled sweet bell peppers ripened naturally on the plant under mild spring sun. Vibrant jewel tones of red, yellow, and green.
storageTip: Keep dry in a breathable paper bag in the crisper drawer; avoid washing until ready to dice.

name: Kandahari Ruby Pomegranates (Anaar)
description: Lustrous crimson arils brimming with tart-sweet ruby juice. Grown in arid hillside orchards and harvested at complete sugar maturity.
storageTip: Whole pomegranates keep at room temperature for 10 days, or refrigerated for up to a month.

name: Chaunsa Honey Summer Mangoes
description: The world-famous aromatic golden mango known for its intense floral honeyed bouquet and rich, melt-in-mouth juicy sweetness.
storageTip: Submerge in cold well water for an hour before peeling and serving chilled for the authentic regional experience.

name: Fresh Swat Golden Apricots (Khubani)
description: Delicate golden-orange stone fruits with velvety skin and sweet musky flesh. Hand-picked in northern valleys and brought down by cooperative transport.
storageTip: Leave at room temperature until fragrant, then chill in a single layer in the refrigerator.

name: Sun-Ripened Purple Figs (Anjeer)
description: Soft, voluptuous deep purple figs with pink honey-sweet jammy centers. Highly perishable and harvested hours before market arrival.
storageTip: Enjoy within 48 hours of purchase. Keep refrigerated in a paper-lined tray without stacking.

name: Wild Rosemary & Fresh Lemongrass
description: Resinous wild pine needles of mountain rosemary paired with crisp citrusy lemongrass stalks. Perfect for herbal teas and artisan roast marinades.
storageTip: Wrap rosemary in slightly damp paper towels inside a sealed container; keep lemongrass standing in a cup of water.

name: Kasuri Fenugreek (Methi) & Fragrant Dill
description: Distinctive small green leaves with rich bitter-sweet herbal fragrance alongside feathery green dill sprigs for authentic regional winter cooking.
storageTip: Wash thoroughly to remove garden loam, pat dry completely, and freeze in sealed bags or keep chilled in cotton towels.

name: Raw Farm Buffalo Mozzarella & Desi Paneer
description: Creamy, pillowy white cheese handcrafted every dawn from grass-fed Nili-Ravi river buffalo milk. Exceptionally rich in natural milk fats and calcium.
storageTip: Keep paneer submerged in lightly salted cold water inside the fridge; change water every 2 days to maintain freshness.

name: Artisan Fig & Seville Orange Marmalade
description: Slow-simmered whole fruit preserves made in small copper cauldrons with wild Sindh figs and bitter seville oranges. Low cane sugar, vibrant flavor.
storageTip: Once jar seal is opened, store in the refrigerator and use clean dry utensils to extend shelf life for up to 3 months.

name: Cold-Pressed Raw Black Sesame (Til) Oil
description: Unrefined virgin black sesame oil expeller-pressed on traditional stone mills. Deep nutty aroma, rich warming character for dressing and herbal care.
storageTip: Keep in a dark glass bottle in a cool dry pantry away from the stove.

name: Stone-Baked Saffron Sheermal & Naan
description: Golden, slightly sweet leavened bread kneaded with farm milk, pure butter ghee, and steeped saffron threads, baked in high-heat clay tandoors.
storageTip: Wrap in cotton roti cloth. Warm on a dry cast-iron skillet for 30 seconds before eating.

name: Roasted Cardamom & Honey Almond Granola
description: Small-batch oven-toasted rolled oats, local whole almonds, pumpkin seeds, and green cardamom pods glazed with raw Sidr blossom honey.
storageTip: Keep in an airtight mason jar in a cool dry spot to preserve satisfying snap and crunch.
